title: LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon with an 8.7σ global significance
summary: Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon. The reported mass is 3725.9 ± 1.0 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) ± 0.4 (lifetime) ± 0.6 (external) MeV/c². A boosted decision tree suppressed random-track combinatorial background; the result is a preprint submitted to Physical Review Letters.

evidence.tested: Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon.
evidence.unknown: The source is an LHCb collaboration preprint submitted to PRL, not yet a peer-reviewed journal publication as of its arXiv version. The observed peak has 8.7σ global significance; the mass uncertainty includes an explicit lifetime-dependent selection-bias term because the Ωcc⁺ lifetime is unknown. BDT use is an analysis component, not the sole basis of the observation.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT was trained on simulated Ωcc⁺ signal decays and wrong-charge Ωc⁰π⁻ combinations from data and used to suppress the dominant random-track combinatorial background in the offline candidate selection. The background rejection supported the mass-spectrum analysis yielding the first observation.
